newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish textile company Berdan Tekstil to go public.
newsitem.headline: Turkish textile company Berdan Tekstil to go public.

text.p: Turkish textile producer Berdan Tekstil Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. plans to float part of its capital in mid-March after a series of national and international roadshows, a senior company official said.
The company aims to repay short-term debt with income from the public-offer
"Our main drive in going public was to pay back our short-term credits," Muhtesem Ekenler, president and general manager of the company told Reuters.
The public offer date and price will be set after the company receives approval from the regulatory Capital Markets Board (SPK).
Ekenler and officials from ABN Amro, consortium leader in the public offer, will go on roadshows in London, Paris, Istanbul and Adana in southern Turkey next week.
The company will waive preemptive rights to sell to the public 100 billion lira of new shares which will make up 19.23 percent of its capital.

Berdan Tekstil is an integrated plant with spinning, weaving, dyeing and finishing units and has a product portfolio consisting of polyviscose, including polyester, viscose, wool, linen and their blends.
Berdan Tekstil increased its turnover to 85.6 million Deutsche marks in 1996 from 80.6 million DM in 1995.
Ekenler said the 1997 sale target was a 20.3 percent increase over 1996 to 103 million DM and the 1998 target was 110 million DM.

Berdan Tekstil also targets to increase its exports to 50 million DM in 1997 and 60 million DM in 1998, from 38 million DM in 1996. Its main export markets are European Union countries like Britain, Denmark and Portugal.
The company will spend 12.5 million DM on modernisation investments this year to expand its annual production capacity to 15 million metres from current 13 million.
Ekenler said they concentrated on U.S. and Canada markets through representative companies.
The company reported 441 billion lira of net profits and 4.77 trillion lira of turnover in 1996, up sharply from 57 billion and 2.65 trillion, respectively in 1995.
